Name: Reward Bursts
Author: Cseron
Description:
[size=6][b]Reward Bursts 2.2.0 — focused rewards and persistent jackpots[/b][/size]

[b]New in 2.2.0: Reward history[/b]
Open the Shift+B dashboard and click Reward history to see your last 20 bursts. Click the same button again to return to progress. Each entry shows the in-game date/time, activity, target and actual bonus items with quantity and quality. Normal loot and the jackpot supplement are listed separately within one entry. These are items dropped by the burst, not inventory pickups; original-action loot, XP and quest/kill credits are not included. Empty results are valid, and partial payouts or incomplete tracking are clearly marked.

History survives sleeping but clears when you return to the title screen or close the game. Nothing is written to your save/config, and past rewards cannot be reconstructed. No new settings or balance changes. English and Russian included; Esc and your configured hotkey close either tab.

2.1.1 fixes an update regression: artifact-spot and mine-container action progress always carries over between days, with no additional setting. Current progress and chances are preserved; previously erased progress cannot be recovered.

2.1.0 rebalances standard jackpots and gives wins three brighter, longer-lived vanilla pixel-art waves, a 1.5-second local dim with no pause, slowdown or input block, and the same single explosion cue at a lower pitch. Warm dashboard cards put jackpot information before progress rows and detailed rules.

Combat target rows now use the matching vanilla monster sprite instead of a generic slime. Slimes intentionally share the green-slime family icon; dangerous variants use dangerous sprites where available, with a sword fallback if a texture can't be loaded.

Turn everyday Stardew activities into satisfying loot bursts. Designed for repeat playthroughs: organize your farm, target useful resources, and get meaningful rewards without adding another set of quests, consumables or chores.

[b]Repeatable normal bursts[/b]
Finish a clear action counter, get the normal bonus immediately, and start again. No daily limits and no level-scaled requirements. Only the completed target's counter resets; other targets retain progress.

[b]Independent jackpots[/b]
After each completed normal cycle, the normal reward is paid and then its module's jackpot chance is checked once. Failure adds percentage points; success resets the chance. Chances persist across days and inactivity and never exceed 100%. Jackpot rewards are additional to, not a replacement for, the normal reward. Prize sizes do not grow, and no jackpot date is guaranteed.

[b]Default balance[/b]
[list]
[*]Farming: 10 plants of one crop → 5 full harvests. Jackpot: 50 extra harvests. Starts at 1%, +1 percentage point per failure.[/*]
[*]Foraging: 4 finds → 2 copies of the final find. Jackpot: 30 copies. Starts at 1%, +1 pp.[/*]
[*]Forest: 4 trees, or 4 large hardwood stumps → 2 loot equivalents. Jackpot: 50 equivalents. Starts at 0.1%, +0.1 pp.[/*]
[*]Mining: 4 nodes of one ore → ore from 2 whole extra nodes. Jackpot: ore from 30 nodes. Starts at 0.5%, +0.5 pp.[/*]
[*]Fishing: 4 ordinary rod catches → 2 copies of the last fish. Jackpot: 30 randomly selected eligible fish from the same water. Starts at 0.5%, +0.5 pp.[/*]
[*]Combat: 8 of one supported monster type → 4 independent loot rolls and kill credits. Jackpot: 150 additional rolls and credits. Starts at 0.25%, +0.25 pp.[/*]
[*]Archaeology: 10 artifact spots → 5 independent dig rolls. Jackpot: 50 rolls. Starts at 15%, +15 pp.[/*]
[*]Mine crates and barrels: 10 destroyed containers → 5 independent loot rolls. Jackpot: 50 rolls. Starts at 2%, +2 pp.[/*]
[/list]
Ordinary action progress resets each morning for the six skill modules. Artifact spots and mine containers retain their counters across days until a cycle completes; the next cycle can start immediately with no daily limit. Jackpot chances persist for all modules. Saving follows the normal game rules. All enabled modules work immediately, including at skill level 0 on the first day. No level-up or overnight unlock is needed. All levels use the same thresholds and rewards. Professions, tool upgrades and applicable vanilla modifiers still matter.

[b]Farming and foraging[/b]
Every successful regrowing harvest counts. One blueberry bush is one action, but its bonus is a full independently generated harvest, not just one berry. Each crop has its own counter and all crops share Farming jackpot chance. Junimos, fruit trees, tea and giant crops are excluded; scythe harvesting is configurable.
Foraging combines natural ground and beach finds, spring onions, grown wild-seed crops and optional berry bushes. Extra berries or profession drops do not count as more actions. Truffles, dropped items, cave produce, garbage bins and storage chests are excluded. Wild-seed crops count only as Foraging.

[b]Forest and mining[/b]
Oak, maple, pine and mahogany share a tree pool. Large hardwood stumps are a separate pool sharing the Forest jackpot chance. Leftover small stumps, large fallen logs, explosions and unsupported trees do not count. Final axe destruction and normal professions/Shaving are supported.
Copper, iron, gold, iridium and radioactive ore keep separate counters with one Mining jackpot chance. Pickaxes and player explosions count. Only explicitly supported vanilla ore nodes qualify. Bonus quantity follows whole-node ore rules, including Miner and the dwarf statue; coal, geodes, gems, mystic and modded nodes are excluded. One bomb can legitimately complete several cycles.

[b]Fishing[/b]
Perfect catches are not required. Each successful ordinary rod mini-game counts once, even with multi-fish bait. Normal bursts copy the final fish, including an actually caught legendary fish. Jackpots instead sample weighted local availability using the fishing context, with individual quality. Trash, legendary, limited and story catches are rejected. No equal-probability species list, foreign-water fallback, treasure chest loot, extra bait consumption or synthetic perfect catches. Ponds, traps and festival mini-games do not count.

[b]Combat[/b]
Supported vanilla targets keep their existing distinct types, except slimes share one family. Farm/hutch slimes, event monsters, unknown mod classes and temporary mummy knockdowns are excluded. Bonus loot is independently rerolled, never copied from one lucky rare drop. Every bonus roll gives one Guild/journal/special-order kill credit; it does not create another death or charge Reward Bursts. Burglar's Ring affects loot only, not XP or kill credits.

[b]Archaeology and containers[/b]
The last artifact spot or container supplies the location and table. Treasure Totem spots count. No bias toward undonated artifacts, quest/story reward duplication, bonus trap swarms or limited walnuts. Empty valid rolls are possible and have no guaranteed compensation. Neither module gives bonus XP.

[b]Experience and customization[/b]
Bonus XP is [b]enabled by default[/b] and can be disabled with one global checkbox. It follows successfully processed normal and jackpot equivalents, not arbitrary item-stack totals. Fishing jackpot XP is based on each generated fish. Base totals pass through vanilla gainExperience once per skill, so other XP modifiers apply once. Original action XP stays unchanged.

Press [b]Left Shift + B[/b] for the scrollable progress dashboard: warm jackpot cards first, then target-specific vanilla icons, counters, bars and detailed rules. Combat rows show the relevant monster sprite; slimes share one family icon. Generic Mod Config Menu lets you change each module's switch, threshold, normal/jackpot reward, starting chance and failure increment, plus HUD, sound, XP and collection options. A jackpot uses three longer-lived vanilla pixel waves at 80% opacity: white-gold, module-colored about 80 ms later, then gold about 110 ms later. The world locally dims by up to 45% and fades back over 1.5 seconds without pausing, slowing or blocking input. The optional additional sound is the same single explosion cue at a lower pitch. Ordinary action sounds remain; there are no jackpot sparks, camera shake or full-screen white flash.

[b]Requirements and installation[/b]
Stardew Valley 1.6.15 and SMAPI 4.5.2. Single-player. Generic Mod Config Menu is optional; SpaceCore is not required.
Quit the game and extract RewardBursts into Mods. The archive contains no personal config or game files.

[b]Upgrading from 1.x[/b]
2.0 replaces daily chains, level tiers, daily limits and the perfect-catch option. Standard settings migrate to the new balance. Custom level settings explicitly use their level-1 values and log a warning; custom fixed archaeology/container rewards remain. General preferences and module switches are preserved. Existing saved chain stages are not converted to jackpot chance. Back up your save and review custom settings, especially the new full-harvest and full-node units.

[b]Upgrading from 2.0.0[/b]
2.0.1 removes the skill-level unlock requirement. Old saved locks are ignored immediately; existing counters, jackpot chances and settings remain. No new save or configuration reset is needed.

2.0.2 improves dashboard hotkey handling around single-key menu conflicts and repeated presses while Shift remains held. It adds reward_bursts_menu and reward_bursts_input troubleshooting commands. Your hotkey, balance and save progress are unchanged.

[b]Upgrading to 2.1.0[/b]
ConfigVersion 14 changes only exact former standard jackpot values: Farming 100→50, Foraging 50→30, Mining 50→30, Fishing 50→30 and Combat 200→150. Custom values stay unchanged; Forest, Archaeology and Mine Containers remain 50. Counters and accumulated chances are preserved.

Faster resource, XP and combat-goal progression is intentional. Equivalent rewards do not guarantee exactly +50% sale value, and jackpots are designed to be substantial.
